mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates strong economic demand, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over the 20-day horizon in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 4.5% signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in the next 5 days.
failure_condition: If unemployment rises above 4.5% but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When both unemployment rate decreases and payroll employment increases, it indicates a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If both UNRATE decreases and PAYEMS increases but S&P 500 returns are not positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A high federal funds rate during a monetary tightening cycle leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is above 4.5% but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation as indicated by CPIAUCSL leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL is high but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates strong supply, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO growth is above 2% but S&P 500 returns are not positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When both housing starts and retail sales increase, it indicates strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If both HOUST and RSAFS increase but S&P 500 returns are not positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, a rising unemployment rate indicates labor market tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE rises in late-cycle expansion but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.
